Question: Prediction
Model: BCRAT / Gail model (absolute invasive breast cancer risk)
Architecture detail: Relative risks fitted by conditional logistic regression, applied to race-specific baseline hazards and integrated year by year over the age interval against competing all-cause mortality, which is what converts them into an absolute risk.
Core formula:
A(t₁,t₂) = Σₐ [h₁(a) / (h₁(a)+h₂(a))] · e^(−Λ(a)) · [1 − e^(−(h₁(a)+h₂(a)))]

  h₁(a)  breast-cancer hazard  = RR(a) × race-specific baseline
  h₂(a)  competing all-cause mortality hazard
  Λ(a)   cumulative hazard up to age a
  a      runs year by year from t₁ to t₂
Discrimination (AUC / C-index): we have not read this from the paper yet
Where the equation sits: Not a single printed equation. The relative-risk and baseline-hazard tables (SEER incidence, NCHS mortality) and the year-by-year competing-risk integration are as shipped in the CRAN package BCRA; the integration follows its absolute.risk.R.
How it was verified: CHECKED 2026-08-05 against CRAN BCRA 4 cases via absolute.risk(); worst absolute difference 3.7e-07 percentage points
Where the equation came from: NCI DCEG BCRAT algorithm; relative-risk and baseline-hazard (SEER incidence + NCHS mortality) tables as shipped in the CRAN package BCRA, absolute-risk integration follows its absolute.risk.R
Citation: Gail MH et al. J Natl Cancer Inst. 1989; NCI DCEG BCRAT algorithm
Scope / caveats: Six published Asian-American subgroups collapsed to a single 'asian' stratum using Chinese SEER rates as proxy — a deliberate simplification, documented in the module. Do not use for a specific Asian subgroup without restoring its own hazard vector.

Question: Response
Model: PREDICT Breast v2.2 — adjuvant treatment benefit
Architecture detail: The same parametric survival model evaluated twice, treated and untreated; the difference in survival IS the predicted absolute treatment benefit.
Core formula:
benefit(t) = S_treated(t) − S_untreated(t)

  the same survival model evaluated twice; the difference IS the
  predicted absolute treatment benefit
Discrimination (AUC / C-index): we have not read this from the paper yet
Where the equation sits: Same source as predict_breast (WintonCentre/predictv30r, R/benefits22.R). Absolute benefit is that model evaluated twice, so there is no separate published equation for the response cell.
How it was verified: CHECKED 2026-08-05 — same model and same R comparison as predict_breast.
Where the equation came from: same model as predict_breast — absolute benefit is the difference in cumulative all-cause mortality with vs without the specified adjuvant regimen (chemotherapy generation, endocrine, trastuzumab, bisphosphonate)
Citation: Candido dos Reis FJ et al. Breast Cancer Res. 2017;19(1):58
Scope / caveats: one model occupies two cells; the response cell re-exports the prognosis module rather than duplicating the equation

Question: Prognosis
Model: PREDICT Breast v2.2 (prognosis + adjuvant treatment benefit)
Architecture detail: Parametric survival model with a closed-form log-cumulative-hazard in time, plus additive treatment log-hazard-ratios, one per therapy arm.
Core formula:
S(t) = exp( −H₀(t) · e^PI )

  PI    = Σ βᵢxᵢ  +  Σ log(HR) over the treatments given
  H₀(t) closed form in t, separately for ER+ and ER−
Discrimination (AUC / C-index): we have not read this from the paper yet
Where the equation sits: NOT IN THE PAPER as a closed form. Taken from the MIT-licensed reference implementation WintonCentre/predictv30r, R/benefits22.R -- note this is the UNEXPORTED overall-survival function; the exported benefits222 computes disease-free survival and is a different model.
How it was verified: CHECKED 2026-08-05 against predictv30r:::benefits22 (the UNEXPORTED overall-survival function; the exported benefits222 computes disease-free survival and must not be used)
Top predictor: tumour size, nodes and grade, then treatment
Where the equation came from: MIT-licensed reference implementation WintonCentre/predictv30r, R/benefits22.R — two prognostic indices with ER-stratified fractional polynomials, two published cumulative baseline hazards, additive treatment log-HRs, and year-by-year competing-risk integration
Citation: Candido dos Reis FJ et al. Breast Cancer Res. 2017;19(1):58; model by Paul Pharoah, University of Cambridge
Scope / caveats: v2.2. Radiotherapy terms are present but gated off in the reference (r.enabled = 0) and we mirror that exactly rather than enabling a pathway the reference disables. v3.x not implemented.

Architecture detail: Sex-specific logistic regressions with age-centred predictors and interaction terms; 100 fixed coefficient sets (5 variants x 2 horizons x 5 outcomes x 2 sexes).

    5 variants × 2 horizons × 5 outcomes × 2 sexes
  continuous predictors are age-centred; several enter as interactions

How it was verified: matched applies to the base 10-year model only (Table S25)
Where the equation came from: Khan et al. Circulation 2024 supplemental appendix; all 100 coefficient sets (5 variants x 2 horizons x 5 outcomes x 2 sexes; base 10-year worked example is Table S25)

Question: Prediction
Model: ESC SCORE2
Architecture detail: Cox proportional hazards: 1 - S0^exp(sum of beta*x), followed by a region-specific recalibration on the complementary log-log scale.
Core formula:
risk_uncal = 1 − S₀^exp(Σβx)

  risk       = 1 − exp( −exp( a + b · ln(−ln(1 − risk_uncal)) ) )
  a, b       region-specific recalibration constants (4 ESC risk regions)
Discrimination (AUC / C-index): we have not read this from the paper yet
Where the equation sits: Not in the main text: the article says 'Details of statistical analysis are provided in Supplementary material online, Methods', and the coefficients, baseline survival and the four risk-region recalibration constants live there rather than in a numbered main table.
How it was verified: CHECKED 2026-08-05 against CRAN RiskScorescvd::SCORE2 (MIT) across all four ESC risk regions; agreement within that package's own 1-decimal rounding (it ends in round(x,1))
Where the equation came from: Eur Heart J 2021; Hageman comment 4 d.p. coeff + recalibration table
Citation: SCORE2 working group. Eur Heart J. 2021

Question: Response
Model: LDL-lowering absolute benefit (DERIVED: CTT trial effect x a baseline risk)
Architecture detail: Not a fitted model. A published trial rate ratio raised to the LDL reduction and applied multiplicatively to a baseline absolute risk from another model, yielding absolute risk reduction and number needed to treat.
Core formula:
ARR = baseline_risk × ( 1 − RR^ΔLDL )

  NNT = 1 / ARR
  RR  = 0.78 per 1.0 mmol/L LDL-C reduction   (CTT 2010)
        0.90 for all-cause mortality
  baseline_risk comes from a separate, verified model
Discrimination (AUC / C-index): we have not read this from the paper yet
Developed on: CTT 2010: 26 randomised trials, 169,138 participants, median follow-up 4.8-5.1 years
Where the equation sits: There is no source paper for this model because it is not a published prediction model -- it is a composition this project defined from two published quantities (a CTT 2010 rate ratio and a separately verified baseline risk). The rate ratio's location in CTT 2010 is the only paper citation that applies.
How it was verified: NOT VERIFIABLE BY COMPARISON, and deliberately not claimed to be
Where the equation came from: NOT a published prediction model. A composition of two published quantities: the CTT 2010 rate ratio per 1.0 mmol/L LDL-C reduction (major vascular events RR 0.78, 95% CI 0.76-0.80; all-cause mortality RR 0.90, 0.87-0.93, read verbatim from the abstract, PMID 21067804) applied to an untreated absolute risk supplied by a separate, verified model. ARR = baseline x (1 - RR^delta_LDL); NNT = 1/ARR.
Citation: Cholesterol Treatment Trialists' Collaboration. Lancet. 2010;376(9753):1670-1681
Scope / caveats: The horizon and endpoint are whatever the baseline risk model's were -- this function takes the baseline risk as an argument rather than computing it, so that stays visible. Four assumptions travel with every result: constant proportional effect across baseline risk (which is what CTT reports), a ~5-year trial effect carried to a 10-year horizon, CTT's major-vascular-events endpoint approximating the baseline model's endpoint, and a confidence interval covering the trial effect only, not baseline uncertainty.

Question: Prognosis
Model: GRACE 2003 in-hospital mortality score (acute coronary syndromes)
Architecture detail: Points nomogram: each of 8 predictors is banded and mapped to integer points; the total indexes a published mortality table.
Core formula:
total = Σ points( Killip, SBP, heart rate, age, creatinine,
                  cardiac arrest, ST deviation, cardiac enzymes )

  total → published in-hospital mortality, by lookup
Discrimination (AUC / C-index): C-statistic 0.83 derivation, 0.84 confirmation GRACE, 0.79 GUSTO-IIb
Where the equation sits: Figure 4, the nomogram, plus the points-to-mortality lookup. Arch Intern Med 2003;163(19):2345-2353. Section not captured.
How it was verified: both published worked examples reproduce component-by-component
Where the equation came from: Arch Intern Med 2003;163(19):2345-2353, Figure 4 nomogram — 8 predictors (Killip class, SBP, heart rate, age, creatinine, cardiac arrest at admission, ST-segment deviation, elevated enzymes) plus the points -> in-hospital mortality lookup
Citation: Granger CB, Goldberg RJ, Dabbous O, et al. Arch Intern Med. 2003;163(19):2345-2353
Scope / caveats: GRACE 2003 IN-HOSPITAL mortality only. Not the Fox BMJ 2006 6-month post-discharge score, and not GRACE 2.0 (which replaced the points with a non-linear model). Guidelines citing GRACE 2.0 expect different numbers.

Question: Prognosis
Model: CHA2DS2-VASc (stroke risk in atrial fibrillation)
Architecture detail: Additive integer point score (0-9): one or two points per clinical feature, summed.
Core formula:
score = C + H + 2·A₂ + D + 2·S₂ + V + A + Sc      (0–9)

  C  congestive heart failure      S₂ prior stroke / TIA        (2 points)
  H  hypertension                  V  vascular disease
  A₂ age ≥ 75                      A  age 65–74
  D  diabetes                      Sc female sex
Discrimination (AUC / C-index): C-statistic 0.606 — modest, and lower than several alternatives
Where the equation sits: Chest 2010;137(2):263-272, the point list. Cross-checked against MDCalc's published schema. Table number not captured.
How it was verified: CHECKED 2026-08-05 against MDCalc's published point schema: age <65/65-74/>=75 = 0/1/2, female 1, CHF 1, hypertension 1, stroke 2, vascular 1, diabetes 1
Where the equation came from: Chest 2010;137(2):263-272 — CHF 1, hypertension 1, age>=75 2, diabetes 1, prior stroke/TIA/TE 2, vascular disease 1, age 65-74 1, female 1; total 0-9. Point values cross-checked against MDCalc.
Citation: Lip GYH et al. Chest. 2010;137(2):263-272

Question: Prediction
Model: Cervical CIN2+/CIN3+ logistic models (hrHPV + cytology + age)
Architecture detail: Multivariable logistic regression on hrHPV status, cytology grade and age (optionally E6 oncoprotein) to CIN2+/CIN3+ probability.
Core formula:
logit(p) = β₀ + β_hrHPV·hrHPV + β_cytology + β_age·age
             [ + β_E6·E6 + Σ β_genotype ]

  cytology  7 levels, NILM is the reference and carries no term
  variants  base / +E6 / +genotyping / +both
Discrimination (AUC / C-index): AUC 0.91 (95% CI 0.88-0.93) for CIN2+, base model, cross-sectional validation set
Developed on: Chinese screening population: cross-sectional N=1,915, plus two screening cohorts of 3,179 and 3,082
Where the equation sits: Additional file 1, 'Table S1. - Logistic Regression Parameters'. Main text describes the model under Methods, 'Model development'.
How it was verified: The paper publishes no worked example, no calibration table and no predicted-vs-observed cross-tabulation (checked)
Where the equation came from: doi:10.1186/s12916-021-02078-2 (open access), Additional file 1 Table S1 — four nested logistic models (base / +E6 / +genotyping / full). Base: intercept -3.19059, hrHPV 2.06771, age -0.01935, cytology betas with NILM as reference. Supplement retrieved via the PMC mirror (PMC8414700) after Springer's direct ESM URL returned 403.
Citation: BMC Medicine. 2021;19:237
Scope / caveats: Chinese screening population; outcome is CIN2+/CIN3+ at colposcopy, NOT invasive cancer incidence over time. Genotype groups are the paper's pooled sets and are not interchangeable with other groupings.

Question: Prediction
Model: CRC-PRO (10-year colorectal cancer risk, Multi-Ethnic Cohort)
Architecture detail: Two sex-specific Cox models with different predictor sets, each with restricted cubic splines on five or seven continuous predictors; risk is 1 - S0^exp(Xb) at a fixed 10-year horizon.
Core formula:
risk(10y) = 1 − S₀^exp(Xβ)

  S₀   = 0.9901043  (women)
         0.9846654  (men)
  Xβ   separate models per sex with DIFFERENT predictor sets
  splines on age, education, pack-years, BMI, alcohol
         (+ red meat and activity in men)
Discrimination (AUC / C-index): Cross-validated C-statistic 0.681 (men), 0.679 (women)
Where the equation sits: Table 5A 'Coefficients for the Model Predicting Colorectal Cancer in Men' and Table 5B, the same for women. NOTE: the baseline survival values this library uses (0.9901043 women, 0.9846654 men) are NOT in the paper -- they come from the vendor's R source at ClevelandClinicQHS/riskcalc-website/ColorectalCancer. The paper never states the risk equation 1 - S0^exp(Xb) either; it shows nomograms.
How it was verified: CHECKED 2026-08-06 against the vendor's own deployed R, route 1
Where the equation came from: J Am Board Fam Med 2014;27(1):42-55, doi:10.3122/jabfm.2014.01.130040 (open access, PMC4219857) for the model specification; coefficients from the deployed calculator's published R source at https://github.com/ClevelandClinicQHS/riskcalc-website/tree/main/ColorectalCancer. Two SEPARATE models by sex with different predictor sets (the paper: NSAIDs matter for women only, red meat and activity for men only). Cox form, risk = 1 - S0^exp(Xb), S0 = 0.9901043 women / 0.9846654 men at 10 years; restricted cubic splines on age, education, pack-years, BMI and alcohol in both, plus red meat and activity in men.
Citation: Kattan MW, Cooper GS, Jackson L, Koroukian S. J Am Board Fam Med. 2014;27(1):42-55
Scope / caveats: Multi-Ethnic Cohort (Hawaiian, Japanese, Latino, White, Black; Black is the reference). Validated input ranges enforced: age 45-85, weight 75-350 lb, height 60-80 in, pack-years 0-50, alcohol 0-12 drinks/day, education 6-20 y, red meat 0-5 oz/day, activity 0-4 h/day. Weight and height are IMPERIAL; the spline knots assume the app's own conversion. Note QCancer-10 validates better externally but has no open source.

Question: Prognosis
Model: MSK rectal calculator (RFS + OS after CRT and surgery)
Architecture detail: Cox proportional hazards with restricted cubic splines on age and positive-node count; survival is S0(t)^exp(X*beta) at four published follow-up times.
Core formula:
P(T ≥ t) = S₀(t)^exp(Xβ)

  S₀(t) published only at t = 0, 60, 120, 180 months
  Xβ    restricted cubic splines on age and positive-node count
  RFS and OS use DIFFERENT ypT reference groups
Discrimination (AUC / C-index): C-index 0.70 (95% CI 0.65-0.76) RFS and 0.73 (0.65-0.80) OS, internal validation; 0.71 and 0.72 external
Developed on: 710 patients, Memorial Sloan Kettering, 1998-2014; externally validated at Siteman Cancer Center
Where the equation sits: Supplement 1: the eTable 'Parameter Estimates for Cox Regression Models Predicting RFS and OS' holds the coefficients, and the eFigure 'Predictive Equations for Incomplete Responders for RFS and OS' holds the assembled linear predictors. Main text describes it under 'Development of Clinical Calculators'. Which of the two governs was itself a defect in this project -- settled against MSK's live calculator in favour of the eFigure.
How it was verified: No worked example is published, so parity was established against MSK's own hosted deployment of this model (mskcc.org/nomograms/rectal/post-treatment, whose Supporting Publication block cites this exact paper)
Where the equation came from: JAMA Netw Open 2021;4(11):e2133457, doi:10.1001/jamanetworkopen.2021.33457, Supplement 1 eFigure — full Cox linear predictor and baseline survival S0(t) at 0/60/120/180 months for both RFS and OS endpoints. The eFigure is a rendered image; coefficients read directly from it and re-read from independent PNG renders at 300 and 600 dpi. Cross-checking exp(beta) against the eTable hazard ratios in the same supplement agrees on 6/6 RFS terms and 0/5 OS terms — an internal inconsistency in the published supplement, not a transcription error (see parity_note).
Citation: Weiser MR et al. JAMA Netw Open. 2021;4(11):e2133457
Scope / caveats: Incomplete pathological responders ONLY — complete responders are estimated by Kaplan-Meier in the source tool, not by this equation. RFS and OS use DIFFERENT ypT reference groups (ypT0/T1 vs ypT0/T1/T2). Predictions only at the published S0 grid (0/60/120/180 months); interpolation refused.

Question: Prediction
Model: Kunzmann points model (esophageal adenocarcinoma)
Architecture detail: Points model derived from a stepwise logistic regression, with each coefficient divided by the smallest one, so the integer points ARE the model rather than a lossy summary.
Core formula:
points = Σ round_to_half( βᵢ / 0.40 )      (0–15)

  over age, sex, BMI, smoking, oesophageal condition
  refer for screening if points ≥ 8
Discrimination (AUC / C-index): AUROC 0.80 (95% CI 0.77-0.82); 0.79 internally validated
Developed on: UK Biobank; 355,034 participants aged 50+, 220 oesophageal adenocarcinomas within 5 years
Where the equation sits: Table 2, the points-based model. The points are the fitted coefficients divided by the smallest and rounded to the nearest 0.5 -- the divisor is stated as 0.41 but is provably 0.40 (see the parity test). Section heading not captured.
How it was verified: No worked patient is published and the full text is paywalled, so this was the last model blocked on paper access; the PDF was supplied 2026-08-06
Where the equation came from: Table 2 points-based model — age 0/1.5/2.5/3.5, male 4.0, BMI 0/1.0/1.5/2.5, smoking never/former/current 0/2.0/3.5, esophageal condition 1.5; total 0-15, screening referral at >=8. Points are the fitted coefficients divided by the smallest (0.41), rounded to nearest 0.5.
Citation: Kunzmann AT, Thrift AP, Cardwell CR, et al. Clin Gastroenterol Hepatol.
Scope / caveats: ADENOCARCINOMA only, not squamous cell carcinoma — different disease, different risk factors. UK primary care, age 50+.

Question: Prediction
Model: ABC method (H. pylori antibody x pepsinogen serological groups A-D)
Architecture detail: A 2x2 cross-tabulation, not a regression: H. pylori serology (+/-) crossed with pepsinogen-defined atrophy (+/-) gives 4 ordered groups A-D.
Core formula:
group = H. pylori antibody (±)  ×  pepsinogen atrophy (±)

  atrophy = PG I ≤ 70 ng/mL  AND  PG I / PG II ≤ 3.0
  → groups A, B, C, D, each with a published annual incidence
Discrimination (AUC / C-index): we have not read this from the paper yet
Where the equation sits: Methods, subsection 'Serum pepsinogen level' defines atrophy (PG I <=70 ng/mL AND PG I/II <=3.0); Methods, subsection 'Classification by anti-H pylori antibody and serum pepsinogen status' defines groups A-D; the per-group annual incidence rates are in Table 2.
How it was verified: incidence rates re-derived independently from the paper's own cases and person-years (Tables 1-2): 7/(3324*4.8y)=0.044%/y, 6/(2134*4.7y)=0.060%/y, 18/(1082*4.7y)=0.354%/y, 12/(443*4.5y)=0.602%/y — each reproduces the published rate
Where the equation came from: Gut 2005;54(6):764-768, doi:10.1136/gut.2004.055400, PMC1774550 — group rule from Table 1/Methods (PG+ <=> PG I <=70 ng/mL AND PG I/II <=3.0), annual incidence from Table 2
Citation: Watabe H et al. Gut. 2005;54(6):764-768
Scope / caveats: Japanese cohort absolute rates; ordering transfers, absolute numbers do not. Invalid after H. pylori eradication (seroreversion).

Question: Prognosis
Model: MSK gastric nomogram (disease-specific survival after R0 resection)
Architecture detail: Cox proportional hazards with restricted cubic splines on age, positive nodes, negative nodes and depth of invasion; depth is an ordinal 1-7 entered as a continuous splined term, not as indicators.
Core formula:
DSS(t) = S₀(t)^exp(Xβ)

  S₀ = 0.579053   at 5 years
       0.5089101  at 9 years
  Xβ   splines on age, positive nodes, negative nodes, depth
  references: female, Lauren diffuse, antrum/pyloric
Discrimination (AUC / C-index): Concordance index 0.80, bootstrap-corrected
Developed on: Memorial Sloan Kettering gastric resection series
Where the equation sits: NOT IN THE PAPER as a closed form: J Clin Oncol 2003;21(19) prints a nomogram figure only. Coefficients from ClevelandClinicQHS/riskcalc-website/tree/main/GastricCancer (server.R), with S0 at 5 years (0.579053) and 9 years (0.5089101).
How it was verified: CHECKED 2026-08-06 against the vendor's own deployed R, route 1
Where the equation came from: NOT the paper: J Clin Oncol 2003;21(19) publishes a nomogram figure and no closed-form model. The coefficients come from the deployed calculator's published R source at https://github.com/ClevelandClinicQHS/riskcalc-website/tree/main/GastricCancer (server.R), which riskcalc.org's own page cites to Kattan 2003. Cox form DSS(t) = S0(t)^exp(Xb) with S0 published at 5 years (0.579053) and 9 years (0.5089101); restricted cubic splines on age, positive nodes, negative nodes and depth.
Citation: Kattan MW, Karpeh MS, Mazumdar M, Brennan MF. J Clin Oncol. 2003;21(19):3647-3650
Scope / caveats: Patients after R0 resection for gastric carcinoma. The hosted calculator validates age 25-96, positive nodes 0-23, negative nodes 0-146, size 0.1-21 cm; those bounds are enforced because the splines are only anchored inside them.

Question: Prognosis
Model: Ang 2010 RPA risk groups (HPV / smoking / stage, oropharynx)
Architecture detail: Recursive-partitioning (CART) decision tree: three binary splits on HPV status, pack-years and nodal/tumour stage produce 3 risk groups.
Core formula:
HPV+ ─┬─ ≤10 pack-years ─────────────→ low
      └─ >10 ─┬─ N0–N2a ────────────→ low
              └─ N2b–N3 ───────────→ intermediate

HPV− ─┬─ ≤10 pack-years, T2–T3 ────→ intermediate
      └─ otherwise ────────────────→ high
Discrimination (AUC / C-index): we have not read this from the paper yet
Where the equation sits: Results, subsection 'HPV status and survival', stated as prose and drawn as the recursive-partitioning tree in Figure 2. No table.
How it was verified: CHECKED 2026-08-05 against Fakhry et al. external validation (Cancer 2019;125:2027-2038, PMC6594017), which operationalizes the same risk groups
Where the equation came from: PMC2943767, verbatim Results-section quote — HPV-positive: low risk except smokers (>10 pack-years) with N2b-N3 = intermediate; HPV-negative: high risk except nonsmokers with T2/T3 = intermediate
Citation: Ang KK et al. N Engl J Med. 2010;363(1):24-35 (RTOG 0129)
Scope / caveats: Known ambiguity, documented in code: the primary text uses '>10 pack-years' for the HPV-positive branch's smoking split but 'nonsmokers' (undefined precisely) for the HPV-negative branch's exception. We apply the same <=10/>10 pack-years split to both branches as the more defensible reading; flagged, not silently resolved.

Question: Prediction
Model: aMAP score (5-year HCC risk in chronic hepatitis)
Architecture detail: Linear score on age, sex, ALBI and platelets, rescaled onto 0-100 and banded at 50 and 60; it embeds the whole ALBI score as one term.
Discrimination (AUC / C-index): C-index 0.82–0.87 across aetiologies and ethnicities
Developed on: 11 global prospective cohorts, 17,374 patients with chronic hepatitis
Where the equation sits: The aMAP formula and the 50/60 cut-offs, J Hepatol 2020;73(6):1368-1378 (open access). Exact section heading not captured.
How it was verified: No numeric worked example is published, so parity was established against the custodial calculator hosted by CUHK's Medical Data Analytics Centre, an aMAP collaborating site (mdac.cuhk.edu.hk/calculators/amap/)
Where the equation came from: J Hepatol 2020;73(6):1368-1378, doi:10.1016/j.jhep.2020.07.025 (open access CC BY-NC-ND) — aMAP = ({0.06*age + 0.89*male + 0.48*ALBI - 0.01*platelets} + 7.4)/14.77*100; ALBI = 0.66*log10(bilirubin umol/L) - 0.085*albumin g/L; cut-offs 50 and 60
Citation: Fan R, Papatheodoridis G, Sun J, et al. J Hepatol. 2020;73(6):1368-1378
Scope / caveats: embeds the ALBI score as a term; aMAP rounds ALBI's albumin coefficient to -0.085 where Johnson 2015 uses -0.0852, and each model keeps its own published rounding

points = [albumin < 36 g/L] + [bilirubin > 17 µmol/L]
       + [AFP > 400 ng/mL] + [dominant tumour > 7 cm]

  0 → grade A,  1 → B,  2 → C,  >2 → D
Discrimination (AUC / C-index): we have not read this from the paper yet
Where the equation sits: Point rule (albumin <36 g/L, bilirubin >17 umol/L, AFP >400 ng/mL, dominant tumour >7 cm; grades A-D), Ann Oncol 2013;24(10):2565-2570. Exact table/section not captured.

Question: Prognosis
Model: ALBI grade (albumin-bilirubin liver function)
Architecture detail: Two-term linear score, log10(bilirubin) and albumin, cut at two fixed thresholds into 3 liver-function grades.
Core formula:
ALBI = 0.66 · log₁₀(bilirubin µmol/L)  −  0.085 · albumin g/L

  grade 1  ALBI ≤ −2.60
  grade 2  −2.60 < ALBI ≤ −1.39
  grade 3  ALBI > −1.39
Discrimination (AUC / C-index): we have not read this from the paper yet
Where the equation sits: Results, in the multivariable Cox paragraph, printed inline as 'linear predictor = (log10 bilirubin x 0.66) + (albumin x -0.085)'. The grade cut-offs follow immediately in the same paragraph: 'xb <= -2.60 (ALBI grade 1), more than -2.60 to <= -1.39 (ALBI grade 2), and xb more than -1.39 (ALBI grade 3)'. Table 2 carries the underlying Cox parameters.
How it was verified: CHECKED 2026-08-05 against the primary text (PMC4322258), which prints verbatim: linear predictor = (log10 bilirubin x 0.66) + (albumin x -0.085), grades at -2.60 / -1.39
Where the equation came from: J Clin Oncol 2015;33(6):550-558, doi:10.1200/JCO.2014.57.9151 — ALBI = 0.66 * log10(bilirubin umol/L) - 0.0852 * albumin g/L; grades at -2.60 and -1.39

logit(p) = β₀ + Σ βᵢ (xᵢ − centreᵢ)

  11 predictors: age, race, education, BMI, COPD, personal and
  family cancer history, smoking status, intensity, duration,
  years since quitting

Question: Prediction
Model: RMI 1-4 (Risk of Malignancy Index, adnexal triage)
Architecture detail: A product, not a sum: ultrasound feature score x menopausal-status score x serum CA125, compared against a single threshold.
Core formula:
RMI = U × M × CA-125           (RMI 4 adds × S)

  U  ultrasound feature score
  M  menopausal status score
  S  tumour-size score, RMI 4 only
  refer above 200 (RMI 1–3) or 450 (RMI 4)
Discrimination (AUC / C-index): we have not read this from the paper yet
Where the equation sits: Four separate papers, one per RMI version (Jacobs 1990, Tingulstad 1996 and 1999, Yamamoto 2009). Per-paper locations not captured.
How it was verified: exact integer arithmetic (U x M x CA125) with no fitted coefficients; all four variants' scoring rules verified against their respective derivation papers
Where the equation came from: RMI = U x M x CA125. RMI 1 (Jacobs 1990, doi:10.1111/j.1471-0528.1990.tb02448.x): U 0/1/3, M 1/3, cutoff 200. RMI 2 (Tingulstad 1996): U 1/4, M 1/4. RMI 3 (Tingulstad 1999): U 1/3, M 1/3. RMI 4 (Yamamoto 2009): adds size term S, cutoff 450.
Citation: Jacobs I et al. Br J Obstet Gynaecol. 1990;97:922-929
Scope / caveats: ROMA is implemented separately as its own entry.

Question: Prediction
Model: ROMA (Risk of Ovarian Malignancy Algorithm, HE4 + CA125)
Architecture detail: Two menopause-stratified logistic regressions on ln(HE4) and ln(CA125); the stratum picks which of the two 3-coefficient models applies.
Core formula:
PI = a + b · ln(HE4) + c · ln(CA-125)

  p  = e^PI / (1 + e^PI)
  separate (a, b, c) and cut-off per menopausal status
Discrimination (AUC / C-index): we have not read this from the paper yet
Where the equation sits: 'Statistical Analysis' section, both indices printed inline: premenopausal PI = -12.0 + 2.38*LN(HE4) + 0.0626*LN(CA125); postmenopausal PI = -8.09 + 1.04*LN(HE4) + 0.732*LN(CA125). The PP thresholds (13.1% premenopausal, 27.7% postmenopausal) are in the same section.
How it was verified: CHECKED 2026-08-05 at the equation level
Where the equation came from: Gynecol Oncol 2009;112(1):40-46, Statistical analysis section — premenopausal PI = -12.0 + 2.38*LN(HE4) + 0.0626*LN(CA125); postmenopausal PI = -8.09 + 1.04*LN(HE4) + 0.732*LN(CA125); PP = exp(PI)/(1+exp(PI)); high risk if PP > 13.1% (pre) or > 27.7% (post)
Citation: Moore RG, McMeekin DS, Brown AK, et al. Gynecol Oncol. 2009;112(1):40-46
Scope / caveats: assay-specific (Architect CA125II, HE4 EIA); cut-offs do not transfer across platforms. Premenopausal discrimination is materially worse (sensitivity 67-76%) than postmenopausal (92%)

Question: Prognosis
Model: MSK ovarian nomogram (5-year survival after primary surgery, bulky stage IIIC)
Architecture detail: Cox proportional hazards with a restricted cubic spline on age; five-level residual-disease term whose reference is the MIDDLE category (0.5-1 cm).
Core formula:
S(5y) = 0.4284861^exp(Xβ)

  Xβ   spline on age, plus grade, histology, platelets, ascites
       and residual-disease diameter
  residual disease reference is 0.5–1 cm, the MIDDLE category
Discrimination (AUC / C-index): we have not read this from the paper yet
Developed on: Memorial Sloan Kettering bulky stage IIIC series
Where the equation sits: NOT IN THE PAPER as a closed form. Coefficients from ClevelandClinicQHS/riskcalc-website/tree/main/OvarianCancerPredictSurvivalAfterSurgforBulkyStageIIICCarc, which riskcalc.org's own page attributes to the cited publication.
How it was verified: Route 1, CHECKED 2026-08-06 against the vendor's own deployed R: the reference script copies the model expression VERBATIM from riskcalc.org's server.R and runs it under R 4.6.1, so the comparison is against their arithmetic rather than our reading of it

Question: Prediction
Model: END-PAC (pancreatic cancer risk in new-onset diabetes)
Architecture detail: Additive integer point score from 3 terms: blood-glucose CATEGORY change, weight change over the year, and age at diabetes onset.
Core formula:
total = ΔBG_category + weight_score + age_score      (−6 … 11)

  ΔBG    category difference, NOT mg/dL   (1–4)
  weight LOSS scores positive             (−6 … +6)
  age    ≤59 → −1,  60–69 → 0,  ≥70 → +1
  ≥3 high risk · 1–2 intermediate · ≤0 extremely low
Discrimination (AUC / C-index): AUROC 0.87 (discovery)
Developed on: Rochester Epidemiology Project; discovery 64 pancreatic cancers vs 192 type 2 diabetes, validation 1,096 with 9 cancers (0.82%)
Where the equation sits: Table 1, titled 'Enriching New-onset Diabetes for Pancreatic Cancer (END-PDAC) score parameters' -- note the table says END-PDAC, not END-PAC. Described under 'Patients and Methods'. The three risk-group cut-offs are never listed together in one sentence, which is the direct cause of this project's <0 versus <=0 ambiguity.
How it was verified: No worked example exists and the only public calculator (endpacscore.com) no longer resolves, so parity was established on the primary source itself
Where the equation came from: Gastroenterology 2018;155(3):730-739.e3, Table 1 (END-PAC score parameters), read from the NIH author manuscript. Three additive terms: blood-glucose CATEGORY difference (range 1-4), weight change over the preceding year (-6..+6, loss scores positive), age at diabetes onset (-1..+1). Total -6..11; >=3 high risk, <0 extremely low risk.
Citation: Sharma A, Kandlakunta H, Nagpal SJS, et al. Gastroenterology. 2018;155(3):730-739.e3
Scope / caveats: Adults with glycemically-defined new-onset diabetes (validation in >=50-year-olds). Enriches an already-selected group; NOT a general-population screen.

Question: Prediction
Model: ERSPC RC3 (DRE-volume, biopsy-naïve)
Architecture detail: Multivariable logistic regression: weighted sum of 3 predictors (log2 PSA, log2 prostate volume, DRE) pushed through a logistic link to a probability.
Core formula:
logit(p) = −1.826
           + 1.024 · (log₂ PSA − 2.0)
           − 1.500 · (log₂ volume_class − 5.4)
           + 0.992 · DRE
Discrimination (AUC / C-index): AUC 0.61–0.77 across validation cohorts
Where the equation sits: Appendix, under the heading 'Formulas used to calculate volume classes and the DRE ERSPC RC risks'. Printed there as lpDRE_ERSPC_riskcalc = -1.826 + 1.024 x (log2(PSA) - 2.0) - 1.50 x (log2(volumeclasses) - 5.4) + 0.992 x DRE, which matches this library's coefficients term for term.
How it was verified: CHECKED 2026-08-05 by extracting the coefficients from SWOP's own Flash calculator (/2011/swf/c03dre.swf)
Where the equation came from: Roobol/PBCG World J Urol 2012 appendix; PMC3321270
Citation: Roobol MJ et al. World J Urol. 2012;30(2):149-155. PMC3321270

Question: Prediction
Model: PBCG (Prostate Biopsy Collaborative Group; no cancer / low grade / high grade)
Architecture detail: Multinomial logistic regression over three outcomes (no cancer, Gleason 6, Gleason 7+), with eight fitted coefficient sets so a record missing prior biopsy, DRE or family history uses the model fitted without it rather than an imputed value.
Core formula:
S₁ = β_low · x        S₂ = β_high · x

  P(no cancer)  = 1 / (1 + e^S₁ + e^S₂)
  P(low grade)  = e^S₁ / (1 + e^S₁ + e^S₂)
  P(high grade) = e^S₂ / (1 + e^S₁ + e^S₂)

  x = [1, log₂PSA, age, African ancestry, + known optionals]
  one of 8 coefficient sets, by which optionals are known
Discrimination (AUC / C-index): AUC 75.5% internal validation, 72.3% external (vs 72.3%/69.7% for PCPTRC 2.0)
Developed on: 15,611 men undergoing 16,369 biopsies at eight North American institutions 2006-2017; validated at three European institutions
Where the equation sits: NOT IN THE PAPER as a closed form. The coefficients are in the deployed calculator's R source, ClevelandClinicQHS/riskcalc-website/tree/main/PBCG, as eight coefficient sets (one per missing-data pattern). Establishing this by parity against that source is what verified the model.
How it was verified: CHECKED 2026-08-06 against the vendor's own deployed R, route 1
Where the equation came from: Coefficients from the deployed calculator's published R source at https://github.com/ClevelandClinicQHS/riskcalc-website/tree/main/PBCG. Multinomial logistic with 'no cancer' as the reference outcome, and EIGHT coefficient sets -- one per pattern of missing prior-biopsy / DRE / family-history data.
Citation: Ankerst DP, Straubinger J, Selig K, et al. Eur Urol. 2018;74(2):197-203
Scope / caveats: Men undergoing prostate biopsy. Predicts high-grade (Gleason 7+) separately from any cancer, which is the actionable question. NOT strictly better than ERSPC RC3: external validation found PBCG improved calibration in White men but OVER-PREDICTED in Black and other groups at most thresholds, so both are kept.

Question: Response
Model: Dutasteride chemoprevention (9 outcomes x 2 arms, benefit and harm)
Architecture detail: Seventeen Cox sub-models: nine outcomes each predicted on and off dutasteride, with restricted cubic splines and per-outcome applicability bounds, so the reported quantity is the treated-minus-untreated difference rather than either risk.
Core formula:
risk = 1 − S₀^exp(score)        per outcome, per arm

  difference = on-drug − off-drug
               negative is benefit, positive is harm
  9 outcomes × 2 arms (ASAP has only the on-drug arm)
Discrimination (AUC / C-index): we have not read this from the paper yet
Developed on: REDUCE trial: men with a prior negative 6- to 12-core prostate biopsy
Where the equation sits: NOT IN THE PAPER as a closed form. 315 coefficients across 17 Cox sub-models, machine-extracted from ClevelandClinicQHS/riskcalc-website/tree/main/ProstateCancerConsideringDutasteride by tests/parity/reference/dutasteride_extract.py.
How it was verified: CHECKED 2026-08-06 against the vendor's own deployed R, route 1
Where the equation came from: Coefficients machine-extracted from the deployed calculator's published R source at https://github.com/ClevelandClinicQHS/riskcalc-website/tree/main/ProstateCancerConsideringDutasteride by tests/parity/reference/dutasteride_extract.py. 17 Cox sub-models (9 outcomes x 2 arms, minus one missing arm), 315 coefficients, each risk = 1 - S0^exp(score) with its own predictor subset, spline knots and applicability bounds.
Citation: Nguyen CT, Isariyawongse B, Yu C, Kattan MW — models for men with a prior negative biopsy considering dutasteride (REDUCE)
Scope / caveats: Men with a prior negative 6- to 12-core biopsy in the past 6 months (REDUCE). Nine outcomes, three of them harms (erectile dysfunction, gynecomastia, urinary tract infection). It reproduces REDUCE's central finding that dutasteride LOWERS overall prostate cancer but RAISES high-grade disease -- a model reporting only the overall reduction would answer half the question. Applicability bounds differ per outcome, so a patient can be answerable for some outcomes and not others; unanswerable ones return None rather than a guess.

Question: Prognosis
Model: UCSF-CAPRA (preoperative recurrence risk)
Architecture detail: Additive integer point score (0-10) distilled from a Cox model; at prediction time it is table lookup and addition, with no regression evaluated.
Core formula:
total = PSA + Gleason + T-stage + %positive-cores + age   (0–10)

  PSA      2.1–6 → 0, 6.1–10 → 1, 10.1–20 → 2, 20.1–30 → 3, >30 → 4
  Gleason  0, 1 or 3 — there is no 2-point level
  0–2 low · 3–5 intermediate · 6–10 high
Discrimination (AUC / C-index): Concordance index 0.66
Where the equation sits: Table 1, 'The UCSF-CAPRA scoring system'. Described in Methods under 'Development of the UCSF Cancer of the Prostate Risk Assessment (UCSF-CAPRA)'. The printed points match this library: PSA 0-4, Gleason 0/1/3 (no 2-point level), T stage 0-1, percent positive biopsies 0-1 at the 34% threshold, age 0-1 at 50.
How it was verified: CHECKED 2026-08-05 against MDCalc's published point schema, entry by entry across all five fields (PSA 5 bands, Gleason 0/1/3 with no 2-point level, T-stage, percent cores, age)
Where the equation came from: J Urol 2005;173(6):1938-1942, PMC2948569 Table 1 — PSA 0-4, Gleason 0/1/3, T-stage 0-1, percent positive cores 0-1, age 0-1; total 0-10
Citation: Cooperberg MR et al. J Urol. 2005;173(6):1938-1942
Scope / caveats: preoperative CAPRA only; CAPRA-S (postoperative, Cancer 2011) not implemented
